nahhas-irab:1-2.t: (تِلْكَ) is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ), in the sense of "these are those", and (آياتُ) is a badal (substitute) for it. It is also possible for «تلك» to be in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) through (نتلو), with «آيات» likewise a badal for it; its being accusative is as when you say: زيدا ضربت ("Zayd I struck").

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤادُ أُمِّ مُوسى فارِغاً): we have already discussed it. It is reported from Faḍāla ibn ʿUbayd: (وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤادُ أُمِّ مُوسى فارِغاً) [Translator's note: the variant form attributed to Faḍāla is not shown in the source; the quotation is identical to the standard text]. (إِنْ كادَتْ لَتُبْدِي بِهِ): from بدا يبدو, "to appear". From Ibn Masʿūd, who said: she was about to say: "I am his mother." [Translator's note: the source has «أنا أمّة»; it is translated as "I am his mother" (أمّه).] Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, she was about to disclose his name because of the distress in her breast. (لَوْلا أَنْ رَبَطْنا عَلى قَلْبِها): «أن» is in the position of the nominative, and the response is omitted because what precedes it indicates it, especially as after it comes (لِتَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
(الْمَراضِعَ) is the plural of مرضع as a broken plural (jamʿ taksīr). Whoever says مراضيع takes it as the plural of مرضاع; the pattern mifʿāl is for intensiveness, and the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) does not enter it to distinguish masculine from feminine, because it does not run parallel to the verb. But whoever says مرضاعة brings the hāʾ for hyperbole, as one says مطرابة ("one much given to rapture"). Al-Farrāʾ said: the hāʾ enters what is praise, meaning the cunning one (al-dāhiya), and what is blame, meaning the beast. This view is wrong according to the Basrans; had it been as he said, the hāʾ would be for the feminine. (مِنْ قَبْلُ) is a "limit" (ghāya); the meaning of ghāya is that it became the limit of the noun when something was omitted from it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: it was given the ḍamma because it is the furthest (ghāya) of the vowels; others said: it was given the ḍamma because the ḍamma does not reach it in its unaltered state. Abū Isḥāq said: the implied form is "before We returned him to her". (فَقالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلى أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُ لَكُمْ): «يكفلونه» is not a response (jawāb); rather it is cut off from what precedes, or in the position of a naʿt (adjective) for (أهل).
(وَهُمْ لَهُ ناصِحُونَ): «له» is not attached to (ناصحين); had that been so, it would be a separation between the ṣila (relative clause) and the relative. We have discussed it in «Sūrat al-Aʿrāf».

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
(وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَاسْتَوى آتَيْناهُ حُكْماً وَعِلْماً وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) (14)
(وَلَمَّا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ): according to Sībawayh it is the plural of شدّة; others said: it is the plural of شدّ; and it is said: it is a singular. Abū Isḥāq reported, in another sūra, that no singular noun on the pattern afʿul without hāʾ is known in the speech of the Arabs except أشدّ; this is a mistake, for the lexicographers have reported إصبع. Abū Isḥāq said: the interpretation of "he reached his أشدّ" is that he attained the full extent of a man's strength. (وَاسْتَوى): the exegetes, among them Ibn ʿAbbās, hold that the meaning of واستوى is that he reached forty years; Abū Isḥāq interpreted it as possibly being, in its literal sense, a description of reaching full maturity. (آتَيْناهُ حُكْماً وَعِلْماً): the learned and wise one is he who acts on his knowledge. (وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ): Abū Isḥāq said: He made the giving of knowledge and wisdom a reward for excellence (iḥsān), because they lead to Paradise, which is the reward of those who do excellent deeds.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (وَدَخَلَ الْمَدِينَةَ عَلى حِينِ غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ أَهْلِها): most exegetes, among them Ibn ʿAbbās, hold that he entered at midday. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: he sought to enter the city at a time when its people were heedless, and he entered it when he knew that of them; then there happened what happened, his killing the man before he had been commanded to kill him, so he asked his Lord for forgiveness and He forgave him. In ordinary speech one says: دخلت المدينة حين غفل أهلها ("I entered the city when its people were heedless"), but one does not say: على حين غفل أهلها. «على» enters in this verse because heedlessness is what is intended, so this became like your saying: جئت على غفلة ("I came upon a moment of heedlessness"), and if you wish you say: جئت على حين غفلة; the verse is likewise. (فَوَجَدَ فِيها رَجُلَيْنِ يَقْتَتِلانِ هذا مِنْ شِيعَتِهِ): mubtadaʾ and khabar. The meaning is: when an onlooker looked at the two of them he would say: this one is of his faction, that is, of the Children of Israel. (وَهذا مِنْ عَدُوِّهِ): that is, of Pharaoh's people. عدوّه means "enemies"; likewise one says of the feminine: هي عدو لك ("she is an enemy to you"). Some Arabs add the hāʾ in the feminine, because according to the Basrans it means معادية ("hostile"), and according to the Kufans because the wāw is "hidden (khafiyya)", so they say. But the wāw is not hidden; rather it is a firm letter. (إِنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ مُضِلٌّ مُبِينٌ): a khabar after a khabar; or, if you wish, «مضلّ مبين» is a naʿt.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: There are two views on it. One is that it has the sense of supplication (duʿāʾ); this is the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, and al-Farrāʾ construed it as meaning: "O Allah, then let me never be a supporter of the criminals." The other view is that it has the sense of a statement (khabar). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that his saying "it is" [the supplication view] is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās. Abū Jaʿfar said: that it be a statement is more fitting and more in keeping with the sequence of the discourse, as one says: لا أعصيك لأنّك أنعمت عليّ ("I will not disobey you, because you have been gracious to me"). This is in truth the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, not what al-Farrāʾ reported, because Ibn ʿAbbās said: he did not make the exception [i.e. say "if Allah wills"], so he was tried; and the exception does not occur in supplication: you do not say: "O Allah, forgive me if You will." The most astonishing thing is that al-Farrāʾ narrated that Ibn ʿAbbās said this, and then reported [the opposite] as his view.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
(فَأَصْبَحَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ خائِفاً) [Translator's note: the source quotes only فَأَصْبَحَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ; the comment refers to خائفاً]: accusative as the khabar of أصبح; or, if you wish, as a ḥāl (circumstantial), with the adverbial phrase in the position of the khabar. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: he feared that someone would see him or discover him; he said: (يَتَرَقَّبُ) means "looking around". (فَإِذَا الَّذِي اسْتَنْصَرَهُ بِالْأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُ): «الذي» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (يَسْتَصْرِخُهُ) is in the position of the khabar; it may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. «أمس», when the alif and lām enter it, becomes fully declinable and is inflected according to most grammarians, though some make it indeclinable (mabnī) even with the alif and lām; when it is annexed or indefinite it is also declinable. The reason for its indeclinability according to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd is that its definiteness is not like the definiteness of declinable nouns, so it had to be indeclinable and not inflected; its final letter was given kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. The doctrine of al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, is that a yāʾ has been dropped from it. The Kufans have two views on it: one is that it is transferred from their saying أمس بخير ("be well in the evening"); the other is that kasra is the natural form of the sīn; this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. Sībawayh and others reported that some Arabs treat أمس as a diptote in the nominative only, and a poet under metrical constraint may do this in the genitive and accusative, as he said: [rajaz] 326-
لقد رأيت عجبا مذ أمسا
(I have seen a wonder since yesterday.)
He made it genitive with مذ for what is past, whereas the good usage is the nominative, and he treated «أمس» in the genitive as it is treated in the nominative according to the second dialect. (قالَ لَهُ مُوسى إِنَّكَ لَغَوِيٌّ مُبِينٌ): الغويّ is the one who fails, that is: because you quarrel with one you cannot overcome.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: (فَلَمَّا أَنْ أَرادَ): «أن» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read (أَنْ يَبْطِشَ) [Translator's note: i.e. يبطُش, with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, as the following comment shows; the source prints both forms identically]. It is a dialect form, except that (يَبْطِشَ) [with kasra] is better known than it, even though the ḍamma is more regular (aqyas), because it is an intransitive verb. (إِنْ تُرِيدُ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ جَبَّاراً فِي الْأَرْضِ): ʿIkrima said: a man does not become a tyrant (jabbār) until he kills two souls. Abū Isḥāq said: الجبّار in the language is the arrogant one who does not submit to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ʿIkrima interpreted the verse as killing two souls just as ʿAṭāʾ interpreted «فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين» ("then I will never be a supporter of the criminals") to mean that it is not lawful for anyone to help a wrongdoer, write for him, or keep his company, and that if he does any of that he has become a helper of the wrongdoers; so much so that he said to someone who asked him for a fatwa: "Throw away your pen and seek your provision from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not be a supporter of the criminals."

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: (وَلَمَّا تَوَجَّهَ تِلْقاءَ مَدْيَنَ): Abū Isḥāq said: that is, he took the road that leads towards Madyan. He said: مدين is a diptote because it is the name of a place (buqʿa). (قالَ عَسى رَبِّي أَنْ يَهْدِيَنِي سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ): Abū Isḥāq said: سواء السبيل is the straight course of the road.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: (وَوَجَدَ مِنْ دُونِهِمُ امْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودانِ): we have mentioned the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās that تذودان means "the two of them were holding back". That is well known in the language: one says ذاده يذوده when he holds him back, and when he leads him, because the meaning of "he led him" is that he held him to what he wants. They were only holding back their sheep because they had no strength for watering, and their sheep would be driven away from the water. (قالَ ما خَطْبُكُما): mubtadaʾ and its khabar. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: what do you intend by holding your sheep back from the water? (قالَتا لا نَسْقِي): that is, we are not able to water (حَتَّى يُصْدِرَ الرِّعاءُ): the reading of the people of Kufa and the people of the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), except Abū Jaʿfar, who read (حَتَّى يُصْدِرَ الرِّعاءُ) [Translator's note: i.e. يَصْدُرَ, with the first vowel fatḥa, as the following explanation shows; the source prints both readings identically], and Abū ʿAmr read likewise. The meaning of the first reading is "until the herdsmen take their livestock away", and the meaning of the second is "until the herdsmen depart"; so the two readings give two meanings, and both are good, except that «يُصدر» fits the meaning better. Abū Ḥātim claimed that the meaning is "until they take their livestock away", and said: it does not mean "until they depart", if Allah wills. «الرعاء» is the plural of راع, as you say صاحب and صحاب. Yaʿqūb said: I was told of a dialect form الرُّعاء with ḍamma on the rāʾ. Abū Ḥātim rejected this form and said: if you put ḍamma on the rāʾ you can only say الرُّعاة with hāʾ. What he rejected is not impossible, just as one says غاز ("raider"), with plurals غزّاء and غزّى [Translator's note: the source writes «غزّا»], with the long and short alif. (وَأَبُونا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ): Abū Isḥāq said: the point of «وأبونا شيخ» is that he is unable to come and water, so we, though we are women, needed to go out and water.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
(فَسَقى لَهُما ثُمَّ تَوَلَّى إِلَى الظِّلِّ فَقالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِما أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ) (24)
(فَسَقى لَهُما): that is, before the time at which they used to water. (ثُمَّ تَوَلَّى إِلَى الظِّلِّ): in the language, الظلّ is that on which there is no sun, and الفيء is that on which there was sun and then it moved away. (فَقالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِما أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ): Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: Moses ﷺ said, "My Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me", and no one among creation was more honoured by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than he; and he was in need of half a date, which he sucked, and his belly clung to his back from hunger.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: (فَجاءَتْهُ إِحْداهُما تَمْشِي عَلَى اسْتِحْياءٍ): ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl reported from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who said: she came having put the sleeve of her shirt over her face, or the sleeve of her shift. Abū Isḥāq said: one also says: she came walking the walk of one not accustomed to going in and out, bashful. (قالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِي يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ ما سَقَيْتَ لَنا فَلَمَّا جاءَهُ): there is an ellipsis in the discourse, that is: so he answered her and went with her. (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ الْقَصَصَ قالَ لا تَخَفْ): the ḍamma was dropped from the fāʾ because of the jussive, and the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: (إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ): that is, one who is strong enough for your work and discharges the trust in it.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: (قالَ ذلِكَ) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. (بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ) is in the position of the khabar; the implied form according to Sībawayh is "between us", and the second [بين] was repeated for emphasis. (أَيَّمَا الْأَجَلَيْنِ) is accusative through (قضيت), and «ما» is redundant. (فَلا عُدْوانَ عَلَيَّ) is a negation of exoneration (tabriya) [i.e. the lā of generic negation]. فلا عدوانٌ عليّ [Translator's note: the source prints the variant with the same vowelling as the standard text; the following explanation shows it is the nominative عُدْوانٌ] is also possible, in two ways: one is that «لا» operates like ليس; the other is that «عدوان» is nominative as mubtadaʾ and «عليّ» is the khabar, as you say: لا زيد في الدار ولا عمرو ("neither Zayd is in the house nor ʿAmr"). (وَاللَّهُ عَلى ما نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: and Allah is our witness to what each of us has contracted with the other.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: ʿĀṣim read (أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ) with fatḥa on the jīm, and al-Aʿmash is reported to have read أو جُذوة with ḍamma on the jīm.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: From al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī: (فِي الْبُقْعَةِ) with fatḥa on the bāʾ [Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowelling]. These are dialect forms. Their saying بقاع (as a plural) points to بَقعة, as one says جفنة and جفان; whoever says بُقعة says in the plural بُقع, like غرفة and غرف. Abū Isḥāq said: بُقعة with plural بقاع is also possible, like جفرة and جفار. He said: (أَنْ) is in the position of the accusative, in the sense of "that: (يا مُوسى)".

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: He said: (وَأَنْ أَلْقِ عَصاكَ) is conjoined to it. (وَلَّى مُدْبِراً): as a ḥāl. (وَلَمْ يُعَقِّبْ): that is, he did not turn round. The implied form is: it was said to him: (يا مُوسى أَقْبِلْ وَلا تَخَفْ). Wahb said: it was said to him: go back to where you were. So he went back, wrapped his cloak around his hand, and the angel said to him: "Do you think that if Allah wished to strike you with what you fear, your wrapping your hand would benefit you?" He said: "No, but I am weak, created from weakness." He uncovered his hand and put it into the mouth of the serpent, and it became a staff again. (إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْآمِنِينَ): [safe] from what you fear.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (وَاضْمُمْ إِلَيْكَ جَناحَكَ مِنَ الرَّهْبِ): the implied form may be: he turned his back in flight out of fear (الرّهب), or he wrapped his hand out of fear. From Ibn Kathīr and al-Jaḥdarī: (مِنَ الرَّهْبِ) with ḍamma on the rāʾ and the hāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. الرُّهُب; the source prints the standard vowelling], and from Qatāda: (مِنَ الرَّهْبِ) with fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the hāʾ, on the original form of the maṣdar. (فَذانِكَ بُرْهانانِ): mubtadaʾ and khabar. Whoever read فذانّك has two construals for it: one is that he made ذلك dual and said ذانّك, while one who said ذانك [did so from ذاك]; and it is said: the doubling of the nūn is a compensation for the alif that was dropped from «ذا», and likewise (وَالَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنْكُمْ) [al-Nisāʾ: 16] and likewise (هذانِ خَصْمانِ) [al-Ḥajj: 19]; this second view is the view of Abū Ḥātim. And it is said: the nūn was doubled to distinguish the nūn that is not dropped because annexation does not occur with it from the nūn that is dropped in annexation. As for فذاناك and فذانيك, there is no justification for them.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
(وَأَخِي هارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِساناً فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِي رِدْءاً يُصَدِّقُنِي إِنِّي أَخافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ) (34)
(فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِي رِدْءاً): accusative as a ḥāl. The meaning of «ردء» is "helper", derived from أردأته, that is, I helped him; ردأته ردءا has also been reported. The plural of ردء is أرداء. Whoever lightens the hamza drops it and casts its vowel onto the dāl, saying: فأرسله معي ردا. (يُصَدِّقُنِي): ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read (يُصَدِّقُنِي) in the nominative [i.e. يُصَدِّقُني]; it is a naʿt for ردء, or it may be a ḥāl. Abū Isḥāq said: whoever puts it in the jussive does so as the response to the request.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: الصرح is any spacious building. (وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُ مِنَ الْكاذِبِينَ): the ẓann here is doubt, so he disbelieved on the basis of doubt, since he had seen of the proofs what would not be obscure to anyone of discernment.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
(عَلا) here is a verb. In other contexts it may be a noun, as when you say: أخذته من على الحائط ("I took it from on top of the wall"), and it may be a particle, as in your saying: على زيد مال ("Zayd owes money"). It may be written with yāʾ when it is a noun or a particle, because its alif turns into yāʾ with a pronoun; it turned into yāʾ only to distinguish it from the fully declinable noun (al-mutamakkin), as in your saying: رأيت عصاه يا هذا ("I saw his staff, you there"). Some Arabs do not turn the alif into yāʾ, as the poet said: [rajaz] 324-
طاروا علاهنّ فطر علاها
(They flew on top of them, so fly on top of her.)
When it is a noun it puts what follows it in the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); it also puts what follows it in the genitive when it is a particle; and when it is a verb it makes what follows it nominative as its agent, or accusative because it is transitive to it. (وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَها شِيَعاً): two objects. The singular of الشّيع is شيعة, which is the faction whose members follow (yushayyiʿu) one another, that is, help one another.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: (بَصائِرَ) is accusative as a ḥāl; the implied form is "and We gave Moses the Book as insights", that is, making things clear. (وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً) is conjoined to (بصائر). The nominative is also possible, in the sense of "for it is guidance and mercy".

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: (وَما كُنْتَ بِجانِبِ الْغَرْبِيِّ): the adjective has been put in place of the noun it qualifies, that is, "on the side of the western mountain".

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: (وَلكِنْ رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ) is accusative as a maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object); so according to al-Akhfash, who said: "but your Lord had mercy on you with a mercy". According to Abū Isḥāq it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is, "for the sake of mercy". According to al-Kisāʾī it is as the khabar of كان. He said: the nominative is also possible, in the sense of "but it is a mercy". Abū Isḥāq said: the nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; the paraphrase that follows fits the accusative] means "but He did that as a mercy".

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: (فَنَتَّبِعَ) is the response to (لَوْلا), that is, "if only" (hallā) [Translator's note: the source has «هيلا», read as هلّا].

nahhas-irab:49-49.t:
(قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِكِتابٍ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ هُوَ أَهْدى مِنْهُما أَتَّبِعْهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) (49)
Al-Farrāʾ said: (بِكِتابٍ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ هُوَ أَهْدى مِنْهُما أَتَّبِعْهُ) in the nominative [i.e. أتّبعُه], because it is a ṣila (here: qualifier) for (كتاب), and كتاب is indefinite. He said: if you put it in the jussive, which is the preferred way, it is as the apodosis of a condition.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: Saʿīd reported from Qatāda, who said: They are the Children of Israel. (وَنَجْعَلَهُمْ أَئِمَّةً): he said: those in charge of affairs. (وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ الْوارِثِينَ): he said: that is, after Pharaoh and his people.

nahhas-irab:54-55.t: (أُولئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ): mubtadaʾ and khabar. Abū al-ʿĀliya said: these are a people of the People of the Book who believed in Muhammad ﷺ before he was sent, and some of them lived to meet him. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: I asked al-Zuhrī about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, (أُولئِكَ يُؤْتَوْنَ أَجْرَهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ): who are they? He said: al-Najāshī and his companions. He sent twelve men, who sat with the Prophet ﷺ, while Abū Jahl and his companions were near them; they believed in the Prophet ﷺ, and when they rose to leave him, Abū Jahl and those with him followed them and said to them: "May Allah disappoint you as a company of riders, and disgrace you as a delegation! You did not wait before believing him. We have never seen a company more foolish or more ignorant than you." They said: (سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ) "We have spared no effort in seeking right guidance for ourselves; we have our deeds and you have your deeds." (وَيَدْرَؤُنَ): from درأت, that is, "I repelled"; that is, they repel harm with forbearance and good speech; and it is said: they repel sins with repentance and seeking forgiveness. (وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ): He praised them for spending from their wealth.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: Condition and requital (sharṭ wa-mujāzāh). تجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء [with tāʾ] is on the basis of the feminine of the collective, and (يُجْبى) [with yāʾ] on the basis of the masculine of the plural. ثمرات is the plural of ثمرة, and ثمر has the plural ثمار.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: (وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ بَطِرَتْ مَعِيشَتَها): it is accusative according to al-Māzinī in the sense of "in its livelihood"; when «في» was dropped, the verb became transitive [i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition]. According to al-Farrāʾ it is accusative as tafsīr (specification), and he said: as you say أبطرك مالك ("your wealth made you insolent") and بطرته; and its parallel, in his view, is (إِلَّا مَنْ سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ) [al-Baqara: 130], and likewise, in his view, (فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْساً) [al-Nisāʾ: 4]. Putting definite nouns in the accusative as tafsīr is impossible according to the Basrans, because the meaning of tafsīr and tamyīz (specification) is that it be a single indefinite noun indicating the genus.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «ونمكّن» in the nominative is also possible, in the sense of "and We establish". (وَنُرِيَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهامانَ): this is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim, and it follows the sequence of the discourse, because before it is «ونريد». The rest of the Kufans read it as ويرى فرعون وهامان ("and Pharaoh and Hāmān see"), and al-Farrāʾ allowed ويري فرعون وهامان in the sense of "and Allah shows Pharaoh and Hāmān". (وَجُنُودَهُما مِنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَحْذَرُونَ): it takes two objects because it is the transitive form of يرى.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: Mujāhid said: (أَفَمَنْ وَعَدْناهُ وَعْداً حَسَناً فَهُوَ لاقِيهِ) is Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and (كَمَنْ مَتَّعْناهُ مَتاعَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) is Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: (وَرَأَوُا الْعَذابَ لَوْ أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا يَهْتَدُونَ). Abū Isḥāq said: the response of «لو» is omitted, and the meaning is: had they been guided, they would not have followed them, and would not have seen the punishment. Someone else said: the implied form is: had they been guided, guidance would have saved them and they would not have come to the punishment.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: (فَعَمِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَنْباءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ): that is, they were bewildered and did not know what to answer when they were asked, when it was said to them: (ماذا أَجَبْتُمُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) [al-Qaṣaṣ: 65].

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: (وَرَبُّكَ يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ وَيَخْتارُ): ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān [al-Akhfash the Younger] said: this is the complete stop (waqf al-tamām), and it is not permissible for «ما» to be in the position of the accusative through (يختار), because if it were in the position of the accusative, nothing would refer back to it. He said: and in this there is a refutation of the Qadariyya. Abū Isḥāq said: «ويختار» — this is the preferred complete stop. He said: it is also possible for «ما» to be in the position of the accusative through (يختار), the meaning being: and He chooses that in which there was good for them.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى أُمِّ مُوسى أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ): if you lighten the hamza, you cast its vowel onto the nūn and drop it, because of its closeness to the vowelless letter, and because the nūn before it was vowelless.

nahhas-irab:71-72.t: (أَفَلا تَسْمَعُونَ): that is, will you not then accept? And after it (أَفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ): that is, will you not then see this clearly?

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: (وَنَزَعْنا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً): it is said its meaning is: from every generation; and in every community there are upright people who will bear witness against people on the Day of Resurrection concerning their deeds. (فَقُلْنا هاتُوا بُرْهانَكُمْ): that is, your proof for what you used to follow as religion. (فَعَلِمُوا أَنَّ الْحَقَّ لِلَّهِ): that is, that the truth is what was in this world [Translator's note: so in the source]. (وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ): that is, what they used to call upon besides Allah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said before this: (وَقِيلَ ادْعُوا شُرَكاءَكُمْ) [al-Qaṣaṣ: 64], that is, those whom you made partners with Allah, Mighty and Majestic — your "partners", because they assigned them a share of their wealth. This is by way of rebuke, that is: call on them to save you from what you are in. So they called on them, but they did not answer them, that is, they did not save them nor help them. This is the meaning of (وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ).

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: «قارون» is a diptote because it is a foreign name; whatever foreign name is on the pattern fāʿūl and does not properly take the alif and lām is a diptote when definite and fully declinable when indefinite; if the alif and lām suit it, it is fully declinable if it is the name of a male, such as طاوس ("peacock") and راقود ("earthenware jar"). Abū Isḥāq said: had قارون been Arabic, from قرنت الشيء ("I joined the thing"), it would be fully declinable. (وَآتَيْناهُ مِنَ الْكُنُوزِ ما إِنَّ مَفاتِحَهُ): إنّ and its noun are within the ṣila of «ما». Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: how ugly is what the Kufans say about the ṣila, that the ṣila of الذي and its sisters may not be «أنّ» and what it governs, when in the Qurʾān there is «ما أن مفاتحه». It is the plural of مفتح; whoever says مفتاح says مفاتيح. (لَتَنُوأُ بِالْعُصْبَةِ): the best that has been said about it is that the meaning is "would weigh down the company", that is, make them bend from its weight, as one says ذهبت به and أذهبته ("I took him away"), جئت به and أجأته ("I brought him"), and أنأته and نؤت به. As for their saying له عندي ما ساءه وناءه ("I have for him what grieves and burdens him"), this is itbāʿ (sound-harmony); it should have been said وأناءه. Similarly one says هنأني الشيء ومرأني ("the thing was wholesome and agreeable to me"), and أخذه ما قدم وما حدث ("what was old and what was new took hold of him"). (إِذْ قالَ لَهُ قَوْمُهُ): al-Farrāʾ interpreted it as Moses ﷺ alone being the one who said it to him, and it was put in the plural; its parallel in his view is (الَّذِينَ قالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ) [Āl ʿImrān: 173], which was only Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd, a man of Ashjaʿ, alone. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say otherwise, rejecting what al-Farrāʾ said because it would nullify clear expression. He said: rather it means that Nuʿaym said it, together with those who followed his way. (لا تَفْرَحْ): Abū Isḥāq interpreted the meaning as "do not exult in wealth", because one who exults in it does not render the due in it. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْفَرِحِينَ): al-Farrāʾ distinguished between الفرحين and الفارحين, claiming that الفرحين are those in a state of joy and الفارحين those who will rejoice in the future, and he claimed that its like is طمع and طامع, and ميّت and مائت. Against what he said stands the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: (إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَيِّتُونَ) [al-Zumar: 30], and He did not say مائت.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: (قالَ إِنَّما أُوتِيتُهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ عِنْدِي): al-Farrāʾ interpreted it in two senses: one is "on account of a merit that I have", and the other is "on account of knowledge, in his view", as you say: هذا كذا عندي ("this is so, in my view"). Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: I was given it only on account of knowledge of the Torah, because he was learned in it; and he rejected the view of whoever said that he used to practise alchemy, saying: because alchemy is false and has no reality.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
«ليكون» is made accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay). This may have puzzled someone ignorant of the language and weak in Arabic, who said: it is not the lām of purpose, and gave it a name whose origin the skilled grammarians do not recognise. Yet this is common in the speech of the Arabs; one says: جمع فلان المال ليهلكه ("So-and-so amassed wealth so that it might destroy him"), جمعه لحتفه ("he amassed it for his death"), and جمعه ليعاقب عليه ("he amassed it to be punished for it"): since his amassing it led him to that, it was as though he had amassed it for that purpose, as the poet said:
[mutaqārib] 325-
فللموت ما تلد الوالدة
(For death is what the mother gives birth to.)
The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read (لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً) [Translator's note: the source does not show the variant form here; the Kufan reading other than ʿĀṣim's is وحُزْناً, which the following comment explains]. This noun is for grief, and الحزن is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of حزن.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: The best that has been said about this is the view of al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, Yūnus, Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī: that the people became aware, or were made aware, and said وي; the remorseful among the Arabs says in his state of remorse: وي. Al-Farrāʾ reported that one of the grammarians said: it is ويك, that is ويلك ("woe to you"), then the lām was dropped. Abū Jaʿfar said: I know of no respect in which this view is not wrong. Among them: the meaning is not sound on it, because the people did not address anyone so as to say to him "woe to you"; and on his view it should have been «إنّه» with kasra on «إنّ», because all the grammarians put kasra on أنّ after ويلك; also, dropping the lām from ويل is not permissible; and also, it is not written thus: ويك [as one word].

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: (مَنْ جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ خَيْرٌ مِنْها): ʿIkrima said: nothing is better than «لا إله إلّا الله» ("there is no god but Allah"); the meaning is only: whoever brings «لا إله إلا الله» will have good (khayr) from it.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t:
(كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ): exception. Abū Isḥāq said: had it been outside the Qurʾān, إلا وجهُه [in the nominative] would have been permissible, in the sense of "everything other than His Face is perishing", as the poet said: [wāfir] 327-
وكلّ أخ مفارقه أخوه ... لعمر أبيك إلّا الفرقدان
(Every brother is parted from by his brother — by your father's life — except the two stars al-Farqadān.)
The meaning is: every brother other than the two Farqad stars is parted from by his brother. (وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ): in the sense of "and you will be returned to Him".

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: (وَقالَتِ امْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِي وَلَكَ): al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "this is a comfort of the eye for me and for you". Abū Jaʿfar said: there is another, far-fetched, way of taking its nominative, mentioned by Abū Isḥāq: it is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (لا تَقْتُلُوهُ). It is far-fetched only because the meaning would become that he is known to be a comfort of the eye to him; its permissibility lies in the meaning being: since he is a comfort of the eye to me and to you, do not kill him. The accusative is also possible, in the sense of: do not kill a comfort of the eye for me and for you. She said "do not kill him (plural)" and did not say "we (shall not) kill him", while addressing Pharaoh, in the way tyrants are addressed and the way they speak of themselves. (وَهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ) may refer to the Children of Israel, or it may refer to Pharaoh's people, that is: they did not perceive that he would strip them of their kingdom.
